memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah near Mamre, in the field of Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite, the field Abraham had bought from the Hittites. There Abraham was buried with his wife Sarah." - Gen 25:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice who stands together at Abraham's grave: Isaac and Ishmael. Years earlier these two half-brothers had been separated — Ishmael and his mother sent away, tension and pain between the families. Yet here, at their father's burial, they come together to honour him. Grief has a way of drawing estranged people back to what matters.

This quiet scene is full of grace. The Bible does not tell us everything that passed between them, but it shows two brothers standing side by side in a moment of shared loss. Old distances do not always have to remain forever.

Is there someone in your family you have grown distant from? Broken relationships are painful, and some wounds are deep. Yet God is a God of reconciliation, and He loves to soften hearts. Sometimes it takes a hard moment — a loss, a crisis — to remind us of what truly binds us.

Through Christ, God has reconciled us to Himself and calls us to be peacemakers (2 Cor 5:18-19; Matt 5:9). We cannot control how others respond, but we can hold our own hearts open. Like Isaac and Ishmael, perhaps we too can stand together again where it counts.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there an estranged relationship God is nudging me to mend?
2. Am I holding my heart open to reconciliation?
3. How has God shown me grace that I can extend to others?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are the God of reconciliation. Soften my heart toward those I have grown distant from, and make me a peacemaker for Your glory. Amen.
